chunks.heading: What is Form PENS.T/2 used for?
chunks.text: Form PENS.T/2 ("Transfer-Out Form") is used to submit an expression of interest to transfer accrued pension rights from UNJSPF to a new employing organization under Article 13 of the UNJSPF Regulations, under the terms of the relevant transfer agreement between UNJSPF and that organization. All pages must be dated and hand-signed, and information should be typed or printed in BLOCK LETTERS.

chunks.heading: What information is required in Section 1 (Participant Information)?
chunks.text: Section 1 requires the Unique Identification Number (UID) (required), pension number (optional), current employing organization index number, full name, date of birth, former employing organization, duty station, phone number, and work email.

chunks.heading: What information is required in Section 2 (New Employing Organization for the Transfer-Out)?
chunks.text: Section 2 requires the name of the new employing organization, date of entry, and the full name, functional title and work email of the point of contact at the new employing organization.

chunks.heading: What do I acknowledge and confirm by signing Section 3 of Form PENS.T/2?
chunks.text: By signing, you confirm that you are interested in transferring your accrued pension rights to the organization named in Section 2; that you have read Article 13 of the UNJSPF Regulations and the relevant transfer agreement; that failing to elect to transfer within the deadline set in that agreement forfeits your right to transfer; that you have read the form's instructions; that you request an estimate of the transfer value; and that the transfer will not proceed unless and until you submit a final election to transfer-out form.

chunks.heading: What note applies to new entrants or re-entrants completing Form PENS.T/2?
chunks.text: New entrants or re-entrants may also be able to validate prior non-contributory service and/or restore prior contributory service under Articles 23 and 24 of the UNJSPF Regulations, provided they apply within one year of their date of entry or re-entry into the Fund, but before separation should they separate earlier.
